attributes.subject: Organises traditional chiefdoms in Cameroon.
attributes.structure: Three classes of chiefdom: first, second and third.
attributes.status_of_chiefs: Traditional chiefs are recognised as auxiliaries of the administration.
attributes.selection: In principle, chiefs are chosen from families that customarily provide the traditional leader.
attributes.related: Order No. 19/CAB/PM of 7 February 1981 lists the traditional chiefdoms.

attributes.titles: Depending on the region, a traditional chief may be called Fo (Fon), Mfo, Lamido, Mey or, in some Muslim chieftaincies, Sultan.
attributes.lamido_regions: Lamido is the title used in the Far North, North and Adamawa regions.
attributes.fon_region: Fon is the title used in the grassfields of the Northwest Region.
attributes.role: A chief has both political and spiritual duties, according to a Canadian refugee board research response.
